outcome.technical: NEW plugins/audit/scripts/governance/_floor_guard.py, a helper with no __main__ that carries PATH_PREAMBLE byte for byte. find_moves(diff, read_base, read_tree, declared=()) -> {answer: FINDINGS|CLEAN|COULD_NOT_TELL, basis, findings[{move,path,line,side,what}], declared[same shape], renamed[{path,from,to,line}], couldNotTell[{path,reason}], notRead[{path,reason}]}. MOVES = test-deleted, definition-changed, skip-added, suppression-added, stub-added. Tables: SKIPS, SUPPRESSIONS, ASSERTIONS. DESIGN DECISIONS: (1) Inputs: git is kept out. The module takes the diff text plus two reader callables (text / None = absent / raise OSError or ValueError = unreadable). It imports no subprocess (case fx1). parse_diff reads git's unified form with a/ b/ prefixes, renames and C-quoted paths. It checks hunk counts strictly; a malformed diff raises _Unparsed and becomes could-not-tell. Each copy is checked line by line against the lines the diff says it added or removed, so a reader returning a different tree is could-not-tell (fc10). (2) Test-file definition: REUSED _filed_returns.is_test_path, not mirrored. The module sits one layer above _filed_returns (new LAYERS entry beside _scope_companions, with a comment) so it can import it. fm22 pins identity (`M.is_test_path is _filed_returns.is_test_path`) and pins behaviour on a path the two existing definitions disagree on (see descriptive). (3) Python definitions: top-level functions plus methods by qualified Class.method (nested classes Outer.Inner.method), compared by ast.dump. ast.dump leaves line numbers out. Decorators are part of the definition (fm5); a leading docstring is dropped (fa6). A name defined twice keeps the last one, which is the one Python runs, so a weaker test appended under an existing name counts as a change. A definition that disappears is a finding unless a new definition with the same body appeared (renamed, fa2). Other languages: assertion lines removed from a test file, read through ASSERTIONS on code-masked text. Moved or reindented lines are paired by exact text (fa8); an assertion rewritten in place reads as removed (fm7). (4) Suppressions are read in COMMENTS only. Python uses tokenize; the c/hash families use a quote-and-comment scanner. So a marker inside a fixture string gives no finding (fa7). Skips and stubs are read on code with strings masked. (5) Pairing: marks are read over both whole copies of a changed file. A tree mark pairs first with a base mark of the same text, then (skips, suppressions, stubs only) with any base mark of the same kind in the same file. So a noqa that moved, or whose line's code changed, gives no finding (fa5). A first draft limited marks to diff regions. I removed that because it was equivalent to whole-file pairing, so no case could pin it. (6) Answers: FINDINGS beats could-not-tell, but couldNotTell is always kept (fc11). With no findings, any could-not-tell is the answer. CLEAN only when nothing failed to read. An empty diff is CLEAN with a basis saying no file changed (fc12); None is could-not-tell (fc9). A file with no known comment syntax (.md) goes in notRead, not silently passed (fa11). (7) declared: entries are `path` or `path::case` (pytest `Class::method` read as Class.method). A non-Python test is declared by file, because its lines map to no case name. OTHER FILES: tools/lints/_deps.py (one LAYERS entry plus comment). outcome.descriptive: A pure, git-free reader now finds the five moves that weaken a test or quiet a checker in a task's diff, with every allow case and every could-not-tell case pinned and each shown red under mutation. OBSERVATIONS for the orchestrator, not fixed (outside this task's files): (a) the plan gate's exemptGlobs in hooks/_config.py count `**/*_spec.*` (rspec's cart_spec.rb) as a test while _filed_returns.is_test_path does not (its name regex has no `_spec` form). The plugin's two test-path definitions disagree, and this module inherits the scripts-side answer (fm22 pins it). (b) This repo's suites group many cases inside one function (`_found(check)` style). Adding a case inside an existing grouping function is therefore a definition-changed finding under the task's per-definition rule, and tests/_harness.py (a test-support path per is_test_path) is compared too. The reporter task should weigh that over-fire risk. (c) Known limits are stated in the module docstring: regex literals in JS, per-file pairing (a suppression carried to another file reads as added), and kind-level pairing cannot see `noqa: <code>` widened to a bare `noqa`.
